chunks: 5464 - It was narrated from Abū Ṭālib ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣalt al-Qummī that he said:

Al-Khalīl ibn Hāshim wrote to Dhū al-Riʾāsatayn, who was the governor of Naysābūr, that a man from the Magians had died and bequeathed something from his wealth to the poor. The executor in Naysābūr took it and distributed it among the poor Muslims. So al-Khalīl wrote to Dhū al-Riʾāsatayn about that, and he asked al-Maʾmūn about it. He said, 'I have nothing on this matter.' Then he asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said:
"The Magian did not bequeath it to the poor Muslims. Rather, an amount equal to that wealth should be taken from the charity funds and returned to the poor among the Magians."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest in his will
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِ: the Magians; the non-Muslim community referred to in the case
key_terms.الْوَصِيُّ: the executor entrusted with carrying out the will
key_terms.فُقَرَاءِ الْمَجُوسِ: the poor among the Magians, the intended beneficiaries in context
key_terms.فُقَرَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the poor among the Muslims, who were mistakenly given the bequest
key_terms.مَالِ الصَّدَقَةِ: charity funds from which compensation is to be taken

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Magian’s bequest to the poor is mistakenly distributed to poor Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the proper execution of a bequest made by a non-Muslim. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام rules that the testator’s intent must be respected, and since the bequest was not meant for poor Muslims, an equivalent amount should be restored to the poor Magians from charity funds.
